newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN INDUSTRIALS END FLAT, GOLDS UNINSPIRED.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN INDUSTRIALS END FLAT, GOLDS UNINSPIRED.

text.p: 1427 GMT - South African industrial shares end flat on Tuesday after earlier gains on a strong overnight Wall Street, which hit record high.
* However, gains in a few heavyweights, including Amic and Minorco , and mining giant Anglo hoisted the all-share index to an all-time best of 7,212.0 -- a gain of 21.6 points

* Golds little changed in thin trade as bullion failed to follow through on overnight gains. Dealers say market hit by futures selling and probably taking a breather after rising in the last few sessions. Volumes traded high and market seen taking its cue from Wall Street on Wednesday.
* Industrials gain 5.3 points to 8,568.7 and golds add 6.6 points to 1,212.3 points.
Edgars shares falls 475 cents to 110 rand after releasing year results below analysts expectations.
South Africa's all-share index rose to a record closing high on Tuesday despite industrial shares being knocked off their highs by expectations of a weaker Wall Street opening.

However, gains in a few heavyweights, including Amic and Minorco , and mining giant Anglo hoisted the overall index to an all-time best of 7,212.0 -- a gain of 21.6 points, the Johannesburg Stock Exchange said.
Gold counters ended only slightly firmer amid thin volumes.
The market started positive after Wall Street gained 143 points to a new record high on Monday night. But futures players combined with weaker S&P futures hit the industrial index.

"The market was very, very choppy. It opened up on the Dow's (overnight) gains but pulled back later. When the Dow looked like it would open weaker the market initially eased but then came back again as Wall Street turned positive," a dealer said.
He said expectations of a weak Wall Street opening on Tuesday hit local industrial shares shortly before the close but they recovered to end flat as Wall Street turned positive.
Volumes traded were worth over 900 million rand, with most blue chips enjoying some interest.
Gold shares ended slightly firmer after bullion gained $3 on Monday. But dealers said volumes were thin and players were concerned that the rise in the bullion price could not be sustained.
"Golds were largely firmer on the back of thin volumes. The market is concerned whether the firmness in gold price will continue," Dominic Rey, international trader at Investec told Reuters.
He added that the gold price was helped in part by the Bre-X Minerals Ltd debacle.
The market was seen taking its cue from Wall Street on Wednesday.
The industrial index ended up 5.3 points at 8,568.7 points and the gold index added 6.6 points to 1,212.3 points.
